identity.title: $\mathbb{H}^{p,q}$-Convex Cocompactness and Higher Higher Teichmüller Spaces
identity.version: Exact acquired source version and hashes will be bound by the6Pro source manifest before dependent review.
identity.actual_source_version: arXiv:2305.15031v7; version-limited author manuscript, no VoR equivalence asserted

summary: An explicit counterexample disproves the general reducible positivity extension and deletion rules used in the core non-degeneracy proof. Two local overstatements have proved restricted repairs; a real quaternionic representation refutes the unrestricted tensor factorization. No main theorem is disproved.

problems.claim: Lemma 6.7 p.52 and Corollary 6.8(2) p.53 assert a positivity extension/deletion rule for potentially reducible representations.
problems.example: G=SL2(R)xSL2(R), Gamma=SL2(Z)xSL2(Z). A=[[2,1],[1,1]], r=(3+sqrt(5))/2. tau1=Sym^2 std_1, tau2=Sym^2 std_2, tau3=std_2. Each is an irreducible real algebraic representation. Sym^2 B always has positive eigenvalue rho(B)^2 >= rho(B) for B in SL2(R), so their direct sum is positively Gamma-semi-proximal. X=lambda(A^2,A) lies in L_Gamma and chi1(X)=4log r>2log r=chi2(X). At gamma=(A,-A^3), which is loxodromic, tau1+tau3 has eigenvalues r^2,1,r^-2,-r^3,-r^-3, hence its sole maximal-modulus eigenvalue is negative. This contradicts Cor.6.8(2).
problems.lemma_example: For the pruned tau=tau1+tau3 use G'={(U,V): all entries U>1 and ||V||_infty<m(U)^2}, where m is minimum row sum. It is nonempty and open, and (A^2,A^2) lies in Gamma intersect G'. Product closure follows from m(UU')>=m(U)m(U') and submultiplicativity of ||V||_infty. Perron-Frobenius gives positive rho(U)>=m(U), so rho(U)^2>rho(V) and tau is positively semiproximal on G'. The same loxodromic gamma refutes the global conclusion. Zariski density follows from the integral upper/lower unipotents in each factor.
problems.proof_failure: In Lemma6.7 the highest eigenspace of tau(a) need not be the highest eigenspace of tau(a') for reducible tau. Closeness of t' to t alone does not preserve the dominant constituent. Benoist Cor.8.5 does not supply that missing control.
problems.impact: The invalid deletion principle is explicitly used in Proposition6.12 Step1 p.55, Step2 p.56 and in Proposition1.13 p.58 via its reference to Step1. Proposition1.13 is a principal ingredient in the closedness results. These proofs require replacement justifications. The counterexample does not satisfy the specialized minimal-dual-constituent configuration of Step1, and does not refute Proposition6.12, Proposition1.13 or the main theorems.
problems.repair: Only the positivity sentence of Step2 can be replaced by positivity of each exposed retained irreducible summand (Cor.6.8(1), independently supported by Benoist Lem.6.3), cone positivity of upsilon, and Remark6.5(2). This does not repair Step1 or all of Step2. No complete core repair verified.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Definition 6.3 and Lemma 6.7 on p.52 contain the loxodromic quantifier and no irreducibility requirement. Corollary 6.8(2), p.53, requires only a strict comparison of chi1 and chi2 at one limit-cone point.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: SL2 x SL2 is connected reductive; integral root subgroups establish Zariski density. The three constituent representations are irreducible and algebraic. X=lambda(A^2,A) is in the limit cone. Gamma contains (A,-A^3), loxodromic in both factors. The open set G' meets Gamma at (A^2,A^2) and is a subsemigroup by the row-sum and operator-norm inequalities.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: For every second factor B, Sym^2 B has positive spectral-radius eigenvalue rho(B)^2 >= rho(B). Thus the full direct sum is positively semiproximal. Deleting that block leaves r^2,1,r^-2,-r^3,-r^-3 at the specified element, with unique negative dominant eigenvalue. On G', rho(U)^2 > rho(V) proves local positivity. The global extension and deletion rule are false.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The counterexample does not instantiate the additional dual-pair minimality setting of Proposition 6.12 Step 1. Benoist's irreducible sign argument is retained; compact-factor approximation does not control which reducible constituent is dominant.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: The p.55 and p.56 invocations and p.58 reference to Step 1 are explicit and feed Proposition 1.13, identified on pp.9-10 as a main closedness ingredient. A false general rule in this core derivation supports Major without asserting a false main theorem.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: The positivity sentence of Step 2 follows from individually positive exposed constituents plus cone positivity and Remark 6.5(2). Neither the entire step nor the core proof is certified repaired.

problems.claim: Proposition3.28(2), p.33, says the boundary extension remains strictly 1-Lipschitz.
problems.example: p=2,q=1; on y0>0 in S^2 put d=y1^2-y2^2 and f=(sqrt((1+d)/2),sqrt((1-d)/2)). It is the p=2 map of Example3.23(ii). Writing theta=0.5 arccos d gives |grad theta|^2=1-y0^2/(1-d^2)<1, so every two interior points are strictly contracted. On boundary y=(0,cos t,sin t), 0<t<pi/2, f=(cos t,sin t), preserving angular distances.
problems.impact: The extension is not strictly contracting on boundary-boundary pairs. The needed interior-boundary inequality remains true by splitting a minimizing geodesic at an interior point and using strictness on the first segment and nonexpansiveness on the second. The proposition is not refuted; the local repair is proved.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: The strict pairwise convention is explicit on p.28, the counterexample is the p=2 specialization of Example 3.23(ii), p.29, and p.33 explicitly asserts strictness of the continuous extension.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: The open upper hemisphere has y0>0 and 1-d^2>0; the displayed map takes values in S1. Every interior geodesic segment stays compactly inside the hemisphere.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Direct differentiation gives |grad theta|^2=1-y0^2/(1-d^2)<1. On the positive-quadrant equator arc, the same map is (cos t,sin t), hence preserves distances.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The application needs an interior-boundary pair, not two boundary points. Splitting at an interior point and applying nonexpansiveness to the remainder proves the required strict inequality.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: The proof sentence is too broad, but the proposition survives the stated local repair; Minor is calibrated.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Interior-boundary strictness is proved; no blanket boundary-boundary strictness is restored.

problems.claim: Proposition5.9 proof p.45 asserts the A_C orbit path for every nonzero a lies in a projective line.
problems.example: j=2,p=2,q=1, x=[1:1:1:1] in the positive crown orthant, a=(1,0). The orbit is [e^t:1:e^-t:1]. First-three-coordinate rows at t=0,log2,log4 have determinant -3/4, hence are not collinear. Hilbert-metric geodesicity is not disputed.
problems.impact: For the directions actually used to form the quadrilateral, all |a_i| are equal, and only two exponential factors occur; those orbits do lie in projective lines. This repairs the overbroad sentence without refuting Proposition5.9 or its application.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Equation (5.1) on p.43 gives diag(e^a1,e^a2,e^-a1,e^-a2); p.45 states projective straightness for every nonzero Cartan direction.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: A two-crown in signature (2,2), x=[1:1:1:1] in the positive orthant, and a=(1,0) satisfy the stated setting. All orbit points remain in the orthant.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: The representative rows at t=0,log 2,log 4 have a nonzero first-three-coordinate determinant -3/4. They cannot lie in one projective line.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The Hilbert-metric geodesic statement is not refuted. The actual four sides on p.45 use directions whose coordinates have equal absolute value.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Only the unrestricted straightness sentence fails. For the used directions two exponential factors give a fixed two-dimensional vector span; Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Restrict to equal-absolute-coordinate directions; this suffices for the stated quadrilateral construction.

problems.claim: Fact6.9 p.53 states an R/C tensor factorization for every irreducible real representation of a product.
problems.example: G=Sp(1)xSp(1), V=H over R, (a,b)x=axb^-1. The representation is real algebraic and irreducible even after restriction to either factor: the orbit of each nonzero quaternion spans H. A proposed tensor decomposition over R or C would force each W_s to have real dimension4 by this restriction, giving dimension16 over R or dimension8 over C, not4. Quaternionic balanced tensor/real-form cases are omitted.
problems.impact: This is a literal general-statement counterexample, also requiring care in the cited Benoist Lemma5.5. It is not a counterexample under the additional semiproximal hypotheses used in Proposition6.12 Step3; generic compact rotations in this example lack real eigenvalues. No central damage from this finding alone is established.
problems.repair: Correct real representation classification or a proved restriction to the needed semiproximal case is required. No full replacement theorem is claimed.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Fact 6.9 on p.53 and the retained Benoist Lemma 5.5(a), p.22, explicitly claim an R or C factorization for every irreducible real product representation.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Unit quaternion groups are connected reductive real algebraic groups. The left-right action on H is real algebraic and irreducible even on restriction to each factor, since a nonzero orbit spans H.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: An R or C tensor factorization with real-irreducible factor modules must, on restriction, have each factor real dimension 4. The resulting dimensions are 16 or 8, not 4. The quaternionic case is missing.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: This compact representation is not G-semiproximal; a nonreal unit quaternion acting on the left has no real eigenvalues. It therefore does not refute the special semiproximal use in Proposition 6.12 Step 3.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: The unrestricted general assertion is false, but no central damage under the additional application hypotheses is established; Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: A corrected real representation classification or proved special-case statement is needed; no complete replacement is certified.

clarifications_and_rejected_candidates.details: If R^{2,1} subset R^{2,q} permits equality, q=1,c=0, v0=(0,5/4,3/4),v2=(0,5/4,-3/4),v1=(1,0,0) with form diag(1,1,-1) meet the unit/pairing/spanning assumptions. The pointwise SO(2,1) stabilizer of v0,v2 is identity, so it cannot move v1 out of R^{2,0}. A strict embedding interpretation excludes q=1; the actual p.71 application already handles q=1 separately and uses q>=2. Do not present this as an unconditional application defect.
The previously suspected c=0 configuration did not satisfy all premises; no confirmed issue is promoted.
